title: Tea country by train
standfirst: The hill country line is slow on purpose. Which stretch to ride, and where to get off.
dek: The hill country line is slow on purpose. Which stretch to ride, and where to get off.

author.name: The Travedise team
author.role: Travel designers in Galle and Bundeena

image.alt: The train crossing the Nine Arch Bridge near Ella

text: The main line from Kandy climbs through tea estates, cloud forest and tunnels on its way to Ella and Badulla. It is not a fast way to travel. That is the point.

The whole run from Kandy to Ella takes most of a day. We usually suggest the second half: board at Nanu Oya, the station for Nuwara Eliya, and ride to Ella. It is about three hours, and it is the most beautiful part of the line.
Your driver takes the luggage by road and meets you at the other end, so you travel with a day bag and nothing else.

body.caption: Where to get on and off
rows: Tea estates and the high passes
The Nine Arch Bridge and the loop

text: Reserved seats in first and second class sell out weeks ahead in the busy months. We book them as soon as your dates are set. The unreserved carriages are cheaper and livelier, but crowded; fine for an hour, hard work for three.

body.text: Sit on the right going up for most of the views. Or stand in the open doorway, like everyone else.

text: Ella is busy now, but the walks around it are not. Little Adam’s Peak is an easy hour at sunrise. The Nine Arch Bridge is best at a train time, when you can watch one cross. We stay just outside the village, where it is quiet at night.

body.label: Weather
body.text: The hills can be misty and wet at any time of year, and the views are best in the morning. The line runs in all seasons, so it fits a route whichever coast you are heading for.
